ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list (required for USD and RAS/SWIFT 'Royalty_Wire' rails); (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) Canada's autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; (iv) the Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 83.05 terrorist-entity listing; (v) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list as secondary diligence. PEP identification must follow FATF Recommendation 12 and FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons guidance, including enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-funds documentation and ongoing transaction monitoring. PRC-sourced corporate and UBO documents must reconcile with SAMR extracts and apostilled notarial records before incorporation filings are submitted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registry portal and ARTS (Alberta Corporate Registration System) through licensed registry agents; mandatory NUANS (New Upgraded Automated Name Search) report obtained within 91 days before incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must use English or French characters and include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'U.L.C.', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' or 'S.A.R.I.' (as permitted). The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to any pre-existing Alberta corporate, extra-provincial or trade name or registered/trademark-protected mark in Canada. Chinese characters are not permitted in the legal corporate name, but a Latin-alphabet transliteration of the Chinese brand (e.g., 'MALATANG' / 'MALA TANG SELF-SERVE BROTH BOWL') is acceptable, provided it is distinguishable and not descriptive to the point of being prohibited. The Chinese-language style name may be registered as a trade name/style and used operationally and on signage subject to municipal licensing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: royal / crown / government / Alberta (suggesting state affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name-search rejection by the Alberta Registrar of Corporations, the applicant may (1) file, within 30 days of the refusal notice, a written name-review request with the Corporate Registry supported by legal argument, a fresh NUANS report, and admissible trademark evidence; (2) reserve an amended distinct name and re-file; (3) if the Registrar upholds the refusal, apply for a statutory review / judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c A-3 and the Alberta Rules of Court, with the corporate name decision as a reviewable administrative act; (4) in parallel, clear contested marks before the Trademarks Opposition Board (CIPO) under the Trademarks Act, RSC 1985, c T-13. An expiring name reservation may be extended for an additional 90-day term by filing a renewal with the prescribed fee before expiry to preserve NUANS priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted. The Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 requires a registered office in Alberta at a physical address (no post-office box) where statutory records are held and process may be served. A licensed Alberta registered agent's virtual office with a physical street address, mail handling and records custody satisfies the Act for the ULC holding/franchise master entity. However, each fast-casual restaurant operation requires its own municipal business licence, Alberta Health Services food-service permit, and physically staffed premises; a virtual office cannot substitute for operational commercial substance at the restaurant level.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: low — approximately 5% annual likelihood of unannounced registry verification. Operational restaurant premises: high — approximately 90-100% annual likelihood of unannounced food-safety inspections by Alberta Health Services under the Food Regulation (Alta Reg 250/2006) and municipal fire/building inspections, independent of corporate registry activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Companies Act, RSA 2000, c C-21, including the provisions governing incorporation and unlimited liability companies. The ULC's articles and liability provisions must be reviewed against the current Act and the Registrar's filing requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction. Filings are submitted through an authorized Alberta registry agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation for an Alberta unlimited liability company, filed with the Registrar under the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum paid-up capital or incorporation escrow deposit applies. The corporation's share structure and subscriptions are set out in its constating documents and subscription records. Banks may impose separate account-opening or source-of-funds requirements. The stated USD filing-fee equivalent is approximate; the government fee is payable in Canadian dollars and registry-agent charges may be additional.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the approved subscription agreements, issue those shares upon receipt of the agreed consideration, and enter the subscribers in the securities register. RESOLVED that the corporation's registered office be established at the Alberta address stated in its filed articles, subject to any required notice of change. RESOLVED that [name] be appointed President and [name] be appointed Secretary, each to hold office until a successor is appointed or the appointment is revoked. RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to complete initial corporate records and make filings necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm ULC eligibility and constitutional terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the proposed entity qualifies for incorporation as an Alberta ULC under the current Companies Act and Registry requirements. Select an available corporate name or determine whether a numbered name is acceptable. Set out the registered office in Alberta, share structure, first directors, and ULC liability terms in the required articles. Obtain Canadian legal and tax advice on the ULC's unlimited shareholder liability and cross-border tax classification before filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-name instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name or documents are rejected or queried, correct the name or articles as directed by the registry agent and resubmit. Confirm ULC eligibility with Alberta counsel before substituting a different entity type.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, via an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed articles and supporting information through the registry agent and pay the applicable government fee and agent charges. Provide original signatures or electronic execution in the form accepted by the agent. Foreign-executed documents may require notarization or authentication if requested; notarization is not a general substitute for the prescribed filing requirements.
required_dossiers: Name reservation or name-search result, if applicable
Agent authorization and identification documents, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond promptly to a deficiency notice through the filing agent, provide corrected forms or supporting evidence, and request reconsideration or resubmission where available. Do not represent the entity as incorporated until the Registrar issues evidence of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board and Alberta Corporate Registry for any required subsequent filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or document unanimous written resolutions. Approve share subscriptions and issuance upon receipt of consideration, appoint officers, adopt the registered-office address, authorize banking, and establish the securities register, minute book, and beneficial-ownership records required by law. File any prescribed notice of directors or registered-office information not completed in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
Securities register and share certificates, if issued
Corporate minute book and required ownership records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete corporate records by properly authorized resolutions and make any overdue registry filings. Obtain Alberta corporate counsel's advice before ratifying actions taken before incorporation or issuing shares.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax and payroll accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, through its Business Registration Online service or prescribed forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register for the applicable corporation income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts based on actual activities and thresholds. Confirm the ULC's federal tax treatment and any cross-border classification elections with tax advisers; Alberta incorporation does not itself establish pass-through treatment for Canadian or foreign tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Payroll and GST/HST registration particulars, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration particulars through CRA channels and respond to verification requests with corporate and identity records. Register before commencing activities that trigger a registration obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general Alberta industrial licensing board issues a restaurant manufacturing permit for this activity. Operational approvals are principally administered by the relevant municipality and Alberta Health Services (AHS); requirements depend on the premises and operating model.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal business licence and AHS food establishment approval or permit, as applicable to the premises and activity. Confirm the exact permit title and application pathway with the municipality and AHS Environmental Public Health before construction or opening.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily not a designated project requiring a full environmental impact assessment under Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act for a standalone restaurant. Separate environmental approvals may apply to site development, wastewater systems, emissions, or other regulated activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No restaurant-specific universal wastewater or VOC threshold is established by this dossier. Obtain municipal sewer approval and comply with applicable wastewater bylaws, grease-interceptor requirements, and provincial approvals. Store and dispose of used cooking oil, food waste, cleaning chemicals, and other controlled waste through compliant systems; comply with applicable environmental approvals and air-emission requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, obtain municipal development, building, plumbing, electrical, and fire approvals applicable to the premises; satisfy Alberta Building Code and fire-code requirements, including any required occupancy approval and fire inspection. Structural load review is required where the building scope or equipment installation warrants it, not as a universal standalone restaurant certificate. Comply with Alberta occupational health and safety requirements, worker training, and food-safety requirements administered by AHS.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal tax administration and Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial tax matters
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities including Unlimited Liability Corporations receive a Business Number (BN) automatically upon incorporation and registration with the CRA. Foreign entities must register with the CRA via the My Business Account portal using Form RC59 if carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment. Required documentation includes articles of incorporation, proof of legal status, and tax classification information.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box elections available under Canadian law. Specific elections exist for hybrid entity treatment, foreign affiliate rules, and certain cross-border structures under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic filing of GST returns through the CRA My Business Account portal. Quarterly filings with digital verification and stamping are required; no real-time API clearance or digital stamping mandate applies, though integration with accounting software for automated compliance is standard.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST rate applies to exports of goods and services performed outside Canada. Eligibility requires proof that the goods are exported or the services are performed outside Canada, such as delivery to a foreign address or performance by non-residents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims result in penalties of up to $10,000 per false statement under the Excise Tax Act, plus interest and potential criminal charges. Retrospective assessments and clawbacks apply for improper zero-rating claims without supporting documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting alongside the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank regulation. Canada maintains no separate foreign exchange administration, exchange control commission, or mandatory capital-import/export licensing agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under a floating exchange-rate regime. Current-account and capital-account transactions are freely executable by Alberta unlimited liability corporations (ULCs) without administrative FX licensing. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted through dividends, royalties, management fees, or interest payments, subject to Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory rate, generally reduced to 10%–15% under the Canada–China Income Tax Agreement). No minimum holding period, no conversion quota, and no repatriation tax apply at the banking level; however, the Income Tax Act s. 212.1 dividend-stripping rules must be respected when subscribing for shares or lending to a related non-resident. Cross-border wires of CAD 10,000 or more are automatically reportable by the financial institution under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) electronic funds transfer reporting regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirements, no statutory conversion timelines, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no retention quotas on export receipts, trade receivables, or royalty/licensing income. Exporters and master-licensing entities may retain foreign currency balances in Canadian or offshore accounts. The only related obligations are balance-of-payments statistical reporting to Statistics Canada (often discharged by the bank) and PCMLTFA reporting of any cross-border EFT of CAD 10,000 or more. A Canadian ULC may transact freely in CNY, USD, or any other convertible currency without prior regulatory approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for use as the primary operational or escrow bank; Medium only as a supplementary low-value disbursement rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise Business, Currencycloud, Nium) do not hold a Canadian Schedule I banking licence, cannot settle directly through Canada's Lynx RTGS or ACSS retail clearing systems, and must rely on Canadian partner-bank sponsorship. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), payment service providers facilitating CAD funds are required to register with the Bank of Canada; an unregistered offshore EMI should not be used for holding franchise escrow collateral or master-license royalty proceeds. The ULC banking strategy must keep the Capital Escrow Account and the primary operational account strictly within a CDIC-insured Schedule I bank to preserve clean audit trails, FINTRAC reporting, and Alberta banking-law enforceability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Alberta ULCs with a Canadian-resident director, tier-1 banks permit remote corporate onboarding with enhanced video KYC and electronic signatures. For a non-resident China-domiciled director, the standard underwriting rule requires at least one in-person visit by a director or authorized signatory to a Canadian branch (Calgary or Edmonton recommended) to satisfy PCMLTFA client-identification rules. Partial remote onboarding is possible when the non-resident director appears via secure video, provides notarized identity documents, and obtains an authorized bank reference; however, the majority of Schedule I banks still mandate a physical appearance for the first corporate account opening. Engaging a Canadian commercial law firm or CPA firm with an established corporate banking desk materially improves onboarding success and may pre-clear the physical-presence requirement through high-net-worth onboarding channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed Alberta ULC with unlimited liability and a tax pass-through election, thin capitalization, and no prior banking or lending history; compliance officers view the structure as unusual and potentially designed for creditor avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) Articles of Incorporation and Notice of Articles; (2) certified Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status; (3) corporate banking resolution and directors' register; (4) complete register of shareholders and ultimate beneficial ownership schedule through to natural persons; (5) specialized outside-counsel opinion on ULC pass-through mechanics, reserve/escrow obligations, and creditor-claims exposure; (6) executed Master License Agreement for the 'Chinese Malatang Self-Serve Broth Bowl' franchise network; and (7) 24-month reviewed financial projections including capital escrow funding and royalty cash-flow forecasts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-domiciled beneficial owner or parent intending to inject CAD 500,000 or more within 30 days of account opening, creating source-of-funds and cross-border anti-money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide enhanced KYC evidence: valid passports/Chinese identity documents, source-of-wealth declaration supported by bank statements or tax records, corporate registry extracts of the Chinese parent, a legal opinion confirming SAFE registration or the lawful cross-border capital path, Chinese anti-bribery/anti-corruption declarations, and the precise wiring sequence showing each intermediary bank. Attach the Investment Canada Act (ICA) notification confirmation generated by the establishment of a new Canadian business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fast-casual restaurant POS revenue co-mingled with master-licensing royalty and escrow flows; processor flags unexpected account turnover and inconsistent transaction narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513 industry classification documents, Alberta food-retail licences, municipal business licensing, Alberta Health Services inspection certificates, executed franchisee unit leases, the Master Licensing Program operations manual, PCI-DSS compliant POS merchant agreements (Moneris, Square, or Stripe), and a treasury segregation SOP showing daily POS sweeps from the operational account to the Capital Escrow Account and then onward to the royalty account at defined calendar intervals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound SWIFT MT103 wires from Chinese banks using vague purpose codes ('Investment' or 'Loan') without documentary trace to the registered ICA filing or the franchise master-license agreement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardize every wire with the correct commercial purpose code: `INVS` for capital injection, `SALE` for trade-related disbursements, or `ROYL` for royalty payments; attach the executed franchise licence, royalty calculation certificate (per the operations manual, typically 4% of franchisee revenue), board resolutions approving the remittance, the ICA notification reference, and any applicable FINTRAC or CRA documentary filings. Maintain a cross-border transaction mapping file that reconciles each inbound wire to the Canadian general ledger and to the ULC share-subscription/capital-contribution record.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step 1: file the Investment Canada Act s.12 notification for establishing the new Alberta ULC business and obtain written acceptance, unless the parent qualifies for a treaty/franchise exemption. Step 2: instruct the Chinese remitting bank to transmit through a well-established correspondent channel (RBC Hong Kong, BMO Asia, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, or HSBC Hong Kong) using SWIFT MT103 with a clear CAD amount, the Canadian ULC's CAD IBAN/account number, and purpose code `INVS`. Step 3: before arrival, supply the Canadian bank with the executed board resolution, source-of-funds evidence, and authorized signatory list. Step 4: after settlement, post the injection as contributed surplus or share capital and deposit the funds into the segregated Capital Escrow Account. Step 5: ensure the bank files the FINTRAC electronic funds transfer report for every dispatch or receipt of CAD 10,000 or more. Step 6: if the Chinese parent is a state-owned enterprise, route the transaction only after obtaining the ICA full-review approval; for all non-SOE shareholders, the s.12 notification is sufficient. Step 7: avoid intercompany loans that could attract Part XIII withholding on imputed dividends; if a loan is essential, execute a written term note, set a commercial interest rate, and document cross-border interest remittance with purpose code `LOAN`.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The ULC treasury must operate a three-rail clearing architecture. Rail A: SWIFT MT103 correspondent wires for high-value payments to Chinese vegetable/ingredient suppliers and self-serve equipment manufacturers; CAD is cleared through Lynx RTGS and converted offshore to CNY/CNH at the receiver's chosen settlement tier. Rail B: Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) mandatory for capital equipment imports exceeding CAD 50,000 per shipment from China, using irrevocable, confirmed, at-sight LCs issued by the Canadian bank in favor of Chinese beneficiaries. Rail C: domestic ACSS/EFT for employee payroll, Alberta provincial taxes, and local POS merchant settlement. All franchise-royalty receipts from Canadian franchisees are settled monthly to the 'Royalty Wire' operational account; no POS cash-flow mixing is permitted. For outward wires exceeding CAD 10,000, the Canadian bank automatically files the FINTRAC EFT report. All CAD/CNY conversions are executed only at the Schedule I corporate FX desk, with the conversion record matched to the underlying trade invoice or royalty certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/CNY FX forwards (tenors up to 24 months) executed under a Canadian FX Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank;

Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the offshore CNH fixing for USD/CAD and CNH/CAD crosses, used exclusively to hedge franchisor royalty income from Chinese master sub-licensees without accessing the onshore CNY deliverable market;
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/CNY) for converting a Chinese parent's capital injection into CAD and for locking fixed exchange rates on planned intercompany capital flows;
European-style CAD/CNY currency options (call spreads and collars) to protect the franchise master royalty margin while preserving upside from CAD appreciation;
Outright CAD/CNY FX swaps on a spot-forward ladder for staged working-capital funding and escrow deployment;

CME-listed CAD/USD futures or FXC CAD/CNH futures in a segregated futures brokerage account, permitted only when the notional exposure exceeds 25% of projected annual royalty/net revenue and the hedge is documented in the ULC treasury and risk-management policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Business Corporations Act annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Ministry of Treasury Board and Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure followed by persistent default can lead to administrative strike-off or dissolution; reinstatement requires court order or registrar reinstatement and payment of arrears and fees; no lawful corporate activity until restored

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food service establishment license and food handling permit renewal (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal licensing authority and Alberta Health Services or regional health authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal before expiry per municipal bylaw; generally 30 days before license expiry or municipal calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of food license, stop-service order, administrative fines, and prosecution under Alberta Public Health Act and municipal bylaws

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of individuals with significant control (ISC) register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained in corporate records; provided to Alberta Corporate Registry upon demand or inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing with mandatory 15-day post-change update; annual reconciliation at fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence-level fines for directors, officers, and the corporation; inaccurate or missing ISC records may also expose the corporation to administrative penalties and compliance orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers an automatic statutory audit under Alberta law. An auditor is required for distributing corporations and any ULC whose shareholders do not unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor. A private non-distributing Alberta ULC may waive audit by unanimous shareholder consent if no shareholder is a public body, no business conducted as a moneylender or trust company, and the corporation is not a reporting issuer; franchise agreements, lenders, or other contracts may nevertheless require a certified audit or review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (Part II); an Alberta ULC may use ASPE if it is a private enterprise, unless designated as a publicly accountable entity or contractually required to report under IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each fiscal year-end, management must reconcile the share-transfer ledger against the Register of Members and inspect all issued, transferred, retired, and reclassified shares for whether any individual has attained or lost 25% or more of shares, votes, or control. Alberta's Business Corporations Act requires the ISC register to be updated within 15 days of a reportable share-transfer or control change. No separate Alberta UBO annual filing is made to the corporate registry, but the ISC record must be available for registrar inspection and should be confirmed during the annual corporate records audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-800 per annum in Alberta for registered office and corporate registry agency services; municipality-specific food business license fees are additional and typically range from USD 80-600
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-12,000 for a full certified audit of a small ULC operating a franchise/restaurant business; USD 2,000-5,000 for a review engagement if audit is validly waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I after abatement and general rate reduction + 8% Alberta general rate). The small business deduction is unavailable because the Alberta ULC is controlled by a non-resident and therefore is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday in Alberta for eating/drinking place franchises. Available federal allowances: SR&ED investment tax credit at 15% for non-CCPCs (35% refundable only for CCPCs, thus unavailable); 100% immediate expensing of certain Canadian-manufactured machinery; accelerated CCA classes (Class 14.1 for franchise licences at 7% declining balance; Class 43/56 for processing equipment). Alberta provincial Innovation Employment Grant (IEG) for qualified Alberta R&D (8% non-refundable credit on first CAD 400,000 of eligible labour). A ULC that elects under ITA s.216.1 as a deemed non-resident loses CCPC-equivalent incentives and computes Canadian-source business income only.
